title: SSC Selection Post Xii 2024 History PART-1

questions.question: Who among the following Mauryan rulers was the first, who tried to convey his messages to his subjects concerning the idea and practice of dhamma through inscriptions?
questions.solution:
• Ashoka and Dhamma: Ashoka
  • Fact: He was the first ruler in world history to use stone inscriptions (edicts) to communicate directly with his subjects about moral codes (Dhamma).

questions.question: The battle of Khanwa was fought between the forces of the Babur and the Rajput forces led by:
questions.solution:
• Battle of Khanwa (1527): Rana Sanga
  • Outcome: Babur defeated the Rajput confederacy led by Rana Sanga of Mewar, solidifying Mughal rule in North India.

questions.question: Gupta emperor Chandragupta I was the first ruler to adopt which of the following titles?
questions.solution:
• Chandragupta I Title: Maharajadhiraja
  • History: This title ('King of Kings') signified the rise of the Gupta Empire from a small kingdom to a major imperial power.

questions.question: Who among the following is associated with the Theosophical Society?
questions.solution:
• Theosophical Society: Annie Besant
  • Legacy: Although founded by Blavatsky and Olcott in NY, Annie Besant became its most famous president in India and founded the Central Hindu College in Varanasi.

questions.question: Which of the following forts was built by Raja Rai Singh in 1588?
questions.solution:
• Junagarh Fort: Junagarh Fort
  • Architecture: Built by Raja Rai Singh in Bikaner, Rajasthan. Unlike most Rajasthan forts, it is not built on a hilltop.

questions.question: Who among the following is NOT associated with the Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha?
questions.solution:
• Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha: Syed Ahmed Khan
  • Context: This was a Parsi reform society founded in 1851. Syed Ahmed Khan was a Muslim reformer (Aligarh Movement).

questions.question: In the reference of the Delhi Sultanate, what was the ‘Group of Forty’?
questions.option_1: They were mostly powerful Turkish slaves of Iltutmish, who took power in the interregnum following Sultana Raziyya's killing.
questions.option_2: They were forty military archers who distinguished themselves by their bravery in the Delhi Sultanate.
questions.option_3: They were forty banjara leaders who transferred military supplies in times of war.
questions.option_4: They were forty Rajput nobles who planned a coup to dethrone Qutb ud Din Aibak in 1210.
questions.solution:
• Group of Forty (Chahalgani): Turkish slaves of Iltutmish
  • Detail: Known as the 'Turkan-i-Chahalgani', this elite corps of 40 slaves was created by Iltutmish to secure his throne.

questions.question: Which of the following cities was the capital of the Pallavas?
questions.solution:
• Pallava Capital: Kanchipuram
  • Culture: Kanchipuram was a great center of learning and a hub for both Shaivite and Vaishnavite temple architecture.

questions.question: Who among the following was the founder of the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science in 1876, an institution, devoted to the pursuit of fundamental research in the frontier areas of basic sciences?
questions.solution:
• IACS Founder: Dr. Mahendra Lal Sircar
  • Fact: This institute is where C.V. Raman later conducted the research that led to his Nobel Prize.

questions.question: The Quit India Resolution was ratified in the _________ session of Indian National Congress to launch the movement.
questions.solution:
• Quit India Ratification: Bombay
  • 1942: The 'Quit India' resolution was passed at the Gowalia Tank Maidan (now August Kranti Maidan) in Bombay.

questions.question: The Federal Court of India was established in Delhi by the Act of ________.
questions.solution:
• Federal Court Establishment: 1935
  • Act: Established under the Government of India Act, 1935. It was the predecessor to the Supreme Court of India.

questions.question: Kalidasa was a famous poet in the court of ________.
questions.solution:
• Kalidasa's Patron: Chandragupta II
  • Nine Gems: Kalidasa was one of the 'Navaratnas' in the court of Vikramaditya (Chandragupta II).

questions.question: Who among the following personalities renounced his knighthood after the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
questions.solution:
• Knighthood Renunciation: Rabindranath Tagore
  • 1919: He returned his title to the British King as a mark of protest against the brutal massacre at Amritsar.

questions.question: Rajasthani architecture is also known as:
questions.solution:
• Maru-Gurjara Style: Maru-Gurjara
  • Architecture: This style originated in Rajasthan and Gujarat, characterized by intricate carvings and ornate domes.

questions.question: Identify the Mughal emperor who was imprisoned for the rest of his life in Agra after the war of succession among his sons.
questions.solution:
• Shah Jahan's Imprisonment: Shah Jahan
  • Fate: He was imprisoned in the Agra Fort by his son Aurangzeb for 8 years until his death.

questions.question: When Akbar introduced Mansabdari system, __________ was the lowest grade of Mansabdar.
questions.solution:
• Lowest Mansabdari Grade: ten
  • System: Mansabs ranged from 10 to 10,000, determining the rank, salary, and military responsibilities of officers.

questions.question: In December 1929, Jawaharlal Nehru, president of Indian National Congress, formally demanded __________ from British Government.
questions.solution:
• Purna Swaraj Demand: complete freedom
  • 1929: At the Lahore session, the Congress moved away from 'Dominion Status' to demand total independence.

questions.question: The first train steamed off from Mumbai to ________.
questions.solution:
• First Train (1853): Thane
  • Distance: Covered 34 km from Bori Bunder (Mumbai) to Thane during the tenure of Lord Dalhousie.

questions.question: Thaneswar where the Vardhana dynasty ruled around the present-day state of ________.
questions.solution:
• Vardhana/Pushyabhuti Base: Haryana
  • Ruler: Harshavardhana's family ruled from Thaneswar (near Kurukshetra) before moving the capital to Kanauj.

questions.question: In which of the following places the Indian National Congress passed the resolution of Purna Swaraj?
questions.solution:
• Lahore Session: Lahore
  • Symbol: The tricolor was hoisted on the banks of the Ravi River at midnight on Dec 31, 1929.

questions.question: Which of the following movement is known as first Satyagraha led by Mahatma Gandhi?
questions.solution:
• First Satyagraha: Champaran movement
  • 1917: Gandhi’s first civil disobedience in India, fighting against the forced cultivation of indigo.

questions.question: At which place is Harappan Dockyard found?
questions.solution:
• Lothal Dockyard: Lothal
  • Archaeology: This Gujrat site contained a massive brick basin that served as the world's earliest known dock.

questions.question: Henry Louis Vivian Derozio, a teacher at Hindu College, Calcutta, in the 1820s, promoted radical ideas and encouraged his pupils to question all authority. Referred to as the ______, his students attacked tradition and custom, demanded education for women and campaigned for the freedom of thought and expression.
questions.solution:
• Young Bengal Movement: Young Bengal Movement
  • Ideology: Inspired by the French Revolution, these students were pioneers of radical intellectual reform in Bengal.

questions.question: Ibn Battuta, who visited India during Delhi Sultanate, originally belonged to which country?
questions.solution:
• Ibn Battuta: Morocco
  • Travelogue: He wrote 'Rihla', documenting his travels across the Islamic world and India during the reign of MBT.

questions.question: Bhabru-Bairat rock edicts mainly depicting Ashokas' conversion to Buddhism is found in _______.
questions.solution:
• Bhabru Edict Location: Rajasthan
  • Significance: It contains Ashoka's explicit declaration of faith in the 'Buddha, Dhamma, and Sangha'.
